job.title: Project Lead (Mechanical) Engineer, Marulan Infrastructure Upgrade
job.description:
Take ownership of the mechanical and structural engineering scope on a significant infrastructure upgrade within a live heavy industrial operation.

This is a hands-on, site-based project leadership role for an experienced Mechanical Engineer who enjoys being close to the work: resolving technical issues, working with contractors and vendors, overseeing installation and ultimately taking mechanical systems through completion, commissioning and handover.

Working within an established capital projects team, you will lead the mechanical discipline across a major upgrade incorporating new crushing and bulk materials handling infrastructure within an operating site.

The opportunity
You will be the key point of accountability for the mechanical and structural scope, taking responsibility from design assurance and equipment procurement through construction, installation, completion and commissioning.

The project incorporates a new impact crusher, screening and conveying systems, stacker reclaimer and stockpile reclaim infrastructure, chute and transfer systems, structural steel, platework, piping and associated plant services. 

Importantly, this is not simply a design engineering position. You will spend significant time in the field working alongside contractors, operations, maintenance and other engineering disciplines to ensure the plant can be safely constructed, commissioned and integrated into an operating facility.

Key responsibilities
  • Own mechanical and structural design assurance across the project.
  • Lead technical review of equipment, drawings, specifications and vendor submissions.
  • Oversee crushing, screening, conveying and bulk materials handling packages.
  • Prepare technical specifications, scopes of work and tender evaluations.
  • Manage vendor technical performance and major equipment procurement.
  • Lead constructability and maintainability reviews with operations and maintenance.
  • Oversee mechanical and structural installation through the site delivery team.
  • Resolve contractor technical queries, NCRs, design changes and site issues.
  • Coordinate mechanical interfaces with civil, electrical and controls disciplines.
  • Manage mechanical interfaces with the operating plant, including shutdowns and tie-ins.
  • Own mechanical completions, punch lists and system turnover packages.
  • Support pre-commissioning, load testing, performance testing and final handover.
The position also has responsibility for a small mechanical team, with approximately 3 direct reports and 3-5 total reports plus contractor supervisory personnel. 

What we are looking for
You will be a practical Mechanical Engineer who has delivered major heavy industrial plant in the field and can comfortably move between engineering detail and construction delivery.  

Ideally, you will bring:
  • Degree qualification in Mechanical Engineering.
  • 10+ years' mechanical engineering experience within resources, quarrying, cement or heavy industrial capital projects.
  • Previous discipline lead or package leadership experience on significant capital projects.
  • Strong experience with crushing, screening, conveying or comparable bulk materials handling plant.
  • Working knowledge of conveyors, transfer points, chutes, structural steel and mechanical equipment.
  • Brownfield construction experience within a live production environment.
  • Experience taking equipment from design and procurement through installation and commissioning.
  • Strong contractor and vendor management capability.
  • Experience managing shutdowns, tie-ins and operational interfaces.
  • Sound mechanical completions and commissioning knowledge.
  • Experience with stacker reclaimers, enclosed stockpiles, cement, lime or quarry operations, offshore equipment sourcing and 3D model reviews will be particularly valuable. 
Why consider this role?
This is an opportunity to take genuine discipline ownership on a major, technically complex brownfield project rather than operating as one engineer within a large design team.

You will have visibility across the full project lifecycle and the ability to influence equipment selection, constructability, installation methodology, commissioning and operational handover.

The role is site based at Marulan for the project delivery phase, providing the opportunity to remain close to the construction and directly influence project outcomes.

job.description:
We are partnering with a major Australian industrial organisation delivering a substantial capital program within an established heavy manufacturing site in the Southern Highlands of NSW. We are seeking an experienced Construction Manager - Site Integration & Commissioning to take responsibility for bringing multiple capital project packages together through final construction, commissioning and transition into operations.
  
This is one of those roles where your title may currently be Construction Manager, Commissioning Manager, Project Manager, Project Engineer or Commissioning Superintendent.
  
What matters most is that you understand what happens on the ground as construction reaches completion and individual systems need to come together, be tested, commissioned and handed over to the operating business.
  
This role is the interface between the site and the project, including procedures, integration with management systems and ultimately commissioning and handover. It is important to note that  while a Project Manager could potentially do the role, its emphasis is much more heavily on construction and commissioning than conventional project management.  
  
What you'll be responsible for
You will coordinate final construction and commissioning activities across multiple project workstreams and ensure systems are ready to safely transition into operations.
  
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Lead site integration across multiple capital project packages
  • Coordinate construction completion and commissioning activities
  • Bring together mechanical, process, electrical and control systems
  • Coordinate contractors and package managers across complex interfaces
  • Ensure systems are ready for testing and commissioning
  • Manage commissioning readiness and completion requirements
  • Coordinate staged tie-ins and shutdown activities
  • Support energisation and plant start-up
  • Coordinate system ramp-up and transition into operations
  • Drive punch-list and defect closure
  • Ensure commissioning documentation and procedures are complete
  • Coordinate closely with engineering, project and operational teams
  • Identify interface risks before they impact commissioning
  • Maintain an integrated view of commissioning progress and readiness
  • Drive contractors toward safe, timely completion and handover
The role ultimately connects the project delivery team with the operating business, ensuring what has been constructed can actually be safely operated, maintained and handed over. This operational interface was specifically emphasised in the client briefing.

The organisation has dedicated safety support, but the Construction Manager remains responsible for ensuring work is safely executed within the live operating environment.
  
What we're looking for - Ideally you will bring:
  • 5-10 years' experience across industrial construction, commissioning or project delivery
  • Strong experience working within a live or brownfield plant
  • Demonstrated commissioning and plant start-up capability
  • Experience coordinating several contractors simultaneously

So who could suit this role? 
We would particularly like to hear from people who have previously been responsible for taking a plant or major industrial system through:  Construction completion → systems integration → commissioning → energisation/start-up → operational handover.  You could currently be working as a Construction Manager | Commissioning Manager | Construction & Commissioning Manager | Commissioning Superintendent | Project Manager | Senior Project Engineer | Integration Manager | Start-Up Manager.

You will bring together multiple project streams and play a key role in ensuring newly constructed assets move successfully from project delivery into reliable operation.  If you enjoy the final, complex stage of major industrial projects, when construction, commissioning, contractors, engineering and operations all converge, then this will be a particularly interesting assignment for you.

Joining an established, purpose-driven national organisation entering an important period of growth, you will help identify and progress potential business transition and acquisition opportunities across a highly regulated services environment. 

This is not traditional transactional sales. There are no hard-sell conversations. 
Instead, you will engage business owners and senior decision-makers, understand their circumstances and future plans, and create the trust needed to explore whether there is a genuine opportunity to work together. 

As the COO describes it: “It is relationship selling. It’s not sales sales. It is about being able to listen.” 

For many of the people you will engage, their business represents years of hard work, deeply established customer relationships and strong connections with their employees and communities. Your role is to understand what matters to them, recognise when the timing may be right and help progress meaningful commercial conversations. 

Why this role? 
  • $90,000–$110,000 + super 
  • Brisbane based hybrid role – 2/3 
  • Newly created position working closely with the COO 
  • Join an established and growing national organisation 
  • Work from an existing pipeline and identified target market 
  • Relationship-led business development rather than aggressive transactional selling 
  • Engage directly with business owners, CEOs and senior decision-makers 
  • Opportunity to contribute to a significant growth strategy 
  • Strong internal support, established market intelligence and existing prospect information 
  • Develop exposure to business acquisitions and commercial transitions

  • Re-engage existing prospects and develop new business opportunities

Your industry background is less important than how you sell.

What matters is that you know how to develop relationships rather than simply push a product. 
You will ask good questions, listen carefully and understand that the strongest commercial outcome may take several conversations to develop. 
You will be comfortable initiating contact and progressing opportunities, but equally comfortable slowing the conversation down when the situation requires it.

  • Demonstrated experience in B2B business development, relationship management or a similar commercially focused role

  • Commercial acumen and the ability to identify genuine business opportunities

  • Ability to tailor your communication style to different people and situations 
  • A genuine interest in working within a purpose-driven organisation 
  • The ability to work independently while remaining highly collaborative 
Previous experience within M&A, corporate advisory, financial services, healthcare or another regulated environment will be highly regarded, however it is not essential. 

The right person may simply be an excellent relationship-based salesperson who understands how to uncover a need, position a solution and build enough trust to progress a significant commercial conversation.

You will be joining a collaborative organisation where strong commercial performance and positive customer outcomes are equally important.

For this reason, being Brisbane based and spending regular time in the office will be important, particularly during your initial onboarding. 
The organisation operates a hybrid working model, with much of the external relationship development conducted through phone, email and video meetings. 
The successful person will be commercially driven, curious and confident, but they will also have the emotional intelligence to recognise that not every conversation should feel like a sales conversation.

job.title: Financial Accounting & Compliance Lead
job.description:
Lead - Financial Accounting & Compliance
Brisbane   12-month fixed-term contract | Circa $170k package + Hybrid work arrangements Financial Accounting | Compliance | Audit | Assurance | Continuous Improvement
Are you an experienced financial accounting professional who enjoys bringing structure, discipline and fresh thinking to established environments?
 
This is an opportunity to join a large, complex and purpose-led organisation in a senior, hands-on financial accounting role with genuine scope to strengthen financial governance, assurance and operating practices.
Working within an established Financial Services function, you will take ownership of core financial accounting deliverables while identifying opportunities to improve processes, strengthen controls, enhance audit readiness and embed more consistent financial practices across a highly decentralised operating environment.
This is not a pure transformation role, nor is it a position where you will simply maintain existing processes. It will suit someone who is comfortable being hands-on technically, while also asking the right questions about why things are done a certain way and where they could be improved.
 
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Lead the preparation and delivery of accurate and timely annual financial statements and support quarterly financial reporting.
  • Oversee core financial accounting activities including balance sheet integrity, reconciliations, accounting treatments and general ledger governance.
  • Coordinate the external audit process and strengthen organisational audit readiness.
  • Proactively manage audit actions, identifying root causes and ensuring issues are appropriately addressed.
  • Provide authoritative technical advice across Australian Accounting Standards, taxation, grants, funding acquittals and financial reporting.
  • Strengthen financial compliance, assurance and control practices across the organisation.
  • Review existing accounting treatments and historical practices, identifying opportunities to improve accuracy and reduce financial risk.
  • Establish more structured and timely approaches to funding and grant acquittals.
  • Support improvements to corporate card governance, compliance monitoring and exception reporting.
  • Act as the financial accounting SME in the review and development of policies, procedures, guidance and training materials.
  • Provide technical financial accounting input into broader systems, payroll and process initiatives.
  • Identify and progress practical continuous-improvement opportunities that reduce errors, strengthen controls and improve service delivery.
  • Coach and develop an emerging accounting professional, building technical capability and confidence.
The environment
You will be joining a large and decentralised organisation with established systems, processes and ways of working.  While the underlying accounting is not unnecessarily complex, the scale and operating model create an environment where consistency, governance and financial stewardship are critical.
There is significant opportunity to review practices that have evolved over time and determine whether they remain appropriate, efficient and compliant.
Success will require someone who can quickly distinguish between:
  • genuine financial and compliance risk;
  • practices that require immediate attention;
  • opportunities for longer-term improvement; and
  • processes that may simply need clearer guidance, controls or communication.
You will need the judgement to challenge the status quo without trying to change everything at once.
 
About you
You will be an accomplished financial accounting professional who combines strong technical accounting capability with sound judgement and an improvement mindset. 
 
You will ideally bring:
  • Strong experience across financial accounting, statutory reporting and year-end.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating external audit requirements.
  • Excellent knowledge of Australian Accounting Standards.
  • Strong balance sheet, reconciliation and general ledger capability.
  • Experience across financial governance, controls, compliance and assurance.
  • Sound taxation knowledge, including exposure to FBT and broader organisational tax obligations.
  • Experience identifying and improving inefficient or poorly controlled accounting processes.
  • The ability to investigate accounting issues and identify their underlying cause rather than simply correcting the immediate problem.
  • Strong written communication and documentation skills.
  • Experience preparing or reviewing accounting position papers, policies, procedures or technical guidance.
  • The confidence to question established practices constructively.
  • Strong prioritisation skills and the ability to focus effort where it will have the greatest impact.
  • A willingness to remain hands-on and technically involved.
  • The ability to coach and support the development of a less experienced accountant.
Experience gained within government, not-for-profit, professional services or even education or any other large governance-led organisation would be advantageous but is not essential.
Candidates coming from a substantial commercial environment will also be considered where they can demonstrate strong financial accounting, governance and compliance capability.
Previous chartered accounting or professional practice experience would also be well regarded.
You will hold relevant tertiary qualifications in accounting, finance, commerce or a related discipline, together with CA/CPA membership or demonstrated progress toward professional membership.
 
What will make you successful?
Technical competence is important, but the strongest candidate will also bring the ability to look at an established financial environment and determine: What is the risk? What actually matters? What should we improve first?
You will be pragmatic rather than theoretical, comfortable working within established governance structures and able to bring others with you as financial practices progressively mature.
Strong written communication will be particularly important, as will your ability to translate technical accounting requirements into practical guidance for stakeholders who may not have a finance background.

Why consider this opportunity?
This is an opportunity to join a stable organisation where the fundamentals are sound, while still having considerable scope to make a visible contribution.  You will have the opportunity to:
  • strengthen audit and assurance practices;
  • improve the quality and consistency of financial accounting;
  • address legacy processes and accounting treatments;
  • strengthen governance and controls;
  • contribute to better systems and operating practices; and
  • build the capability of the financial accounting function.
Importantly, this is not a remediation role within a distressed finance environment. It is an opportunity to take an established function and help lift its maturity.  The position is based in Brisbane's inner south, with the organisation predominantly office-based while supporting some flexibility once established.

job.description:
Project Manager – Major Concrete Operations
Sunshine Coast
Highly competitive Salary – paid relocation costs considered
  
Take ownership of the concrete operations supporting one of the Sunshine Coast’s most significant infrastructure projects and help establish the next operation from the ground up.
Our client is one of Australia’s leading construction materials organisations, with an extensive network of concrete, quarry and operational sites across the country and their people and products support major residential, commercial and civil infrastructure projects, helping to build stronger and more sustainable communities.
Based near Cooroy, you will lead the onsite concrete operations supporting a complex dam improvement project. You will manage plant performance, people, customer relationships, budgets and production delivery, while also helping prepare for an additional project operation at Coolum.
This is not a desk-based project-management position. You will be visible on site, working alongside your team, resolving operational issues and ensuring concrete is produced safely, consistently and in line with demanding project schedules.
This is a permanent position offering exposure to a strong pipeline of major projects beyond the current program.

Your next opportunity
Reporting to the Major Projects Manager for South East Queensland Concrete, you will initially take responsibility for an established onsite operation at Lake Macdonald.

As the project develops, you will also play an important role in establishing and staffing the next concrete operation at Coolum, with the potential to oversee multiple project sites across the Sunshine Coast.

You will lead four direct reports and coordinate approximately 10–15 drivers, working closely with the principal construction contractor, technical teams, suppliers and internal stakeholders.

The environment is fast-moving and highly accountable. Production volumes are significant, customer expectations are high and reliable plant performance is critical to the successful delivery of the broader infrastructure program.
  
Your responsibilities
  • Lead safe, reliable and efficient concrete operations across major project sites
  • Manage daily production requirements against changing project schedules and customer demand
  • Coordinate concrete orders, batching activities, testing and technical support
  • Maintain plant availability and coordinate preventative and reactive maintenance
  • Lead, coach and develop production employees and drivers
  • Create an engaged, accountable and safety-focused site culture
  • Conduct toolbox talks and ensure employees and contractors follow site requirements
  • Build strong working relationships with construction partners, engineers and other stakeholders
  • Respond quickly and professionally to customer concerns and operational issues
  • Manage site expenditure, labour costs, budgets, forecasts and operational performance
  • Monitor production, service, safety and plant-performance targets
  • Drive continuous improvement across plant operations, systems and processes
  • Support recruitment, onboarding and workforce planning for the new project operation
  • Assist with concrete batching and front-end loader operations when required
  • Ensure compliance with all safety, environmental and quality requirements
  
About you
You are an experienced operational leader who is equally comfortable talking with production employees on the plant floor and meeting with engineers and senior project stakeholders.
You remain calm under pressure, communicate clearly and take ownership when production priorities change or problems arise. You understand that strong customer relationships must be supported by safe operations, reliable equipment and consistent delivery.
You will ideally bring:
  • Operational leadership experience within concrete production or a closely related environment
  • A sound understanding of concrete batching, production processes and quality requirements
  • Experience leading plant-based teams in a safety-critical environment
  • Strong customer and stakeholder-management capability
  • The confidence to work directly with construction managers, engineers and project representatives
  • Experience managing production schedules, labour, costs, budgets and operational targets
  • Practical knowledge of plant maintenance, reliability and asset utilisation
  • The ability to balance competing priorities in a high-volume operation
  • A visible and hands-on leadership style
  • Front-end loader operating experience and ideally a current front-end loader ticket
  • A valid Construction White Card
  • A current driver’s license and clean driving record
  
Experience within civil construction, aggregates, quarrying or another heavy production environment may also be considered where you can demonstrate meaningful exposure to concrete operations.
Formal project-management or engineering qualifications are welcome but are not essential. Your operational experience, leadership capability and understanding of concrete production will carry greater weight.
If you do not currently hold a front-end loader ticket but have relevant operational experience and are willing and able to obtain one, we would still welcome a conversation.

Why this opportunity stands out
This role offers considerably more scope than managing a single permanent concrete plant.
You will work at the centre of a significant civil infrastructure project where your decisions directly influence production continuity, customer outcomes and project delivery. You will inherit an established operation, help shape a new site and have the opportunity to build and lead its team.
You will also receive:
  • A permanent, full-time position not a project-based contract
  • An attractive salary package including a tool of the trade vehicle plus relocation assistance if required.
  • A predominantly Monday-to-Friday day-shift roster
  • Exposure to complex, high-profile infrastructure delivery
  • The opportunity to establish and grow additional concrete operations
  • An accessible manager who encourages autonomy and open communication
  • Really positive culture on site
  • Strong technical, safety and operational support
  • Long-term career opportunities across major projects and operational leadership
  • Access to employee support and professional-development programs
  
If you are ready to take ownership of a complex concrete operation, build trusted customer relationships and lead a team delivering an important Sunshine Coast infrastructure project, we would like to hear from you.
